What is Murf?

Text-to-speech studio aimed at business voiceover production - presentations, e-learning, explainer videos and adverts. Built around a timeline editor that syncs voice to slides or video rather than a bare API.

Best for

Business voiceover synced to slides or video by non-audio professionals.

Main features

  • 200+ voices across 20+ languages with style variants (promo, narration, conversational, angry, sad)
  • Murf Studio timeline editor syncing voice to video or slides
  • voice changer converting your recording into a professional voice
  • pronunciation and emphasis controls
  • pitch, speed and pause editing at word level
  • collaboration and commenting
  • Murf API
  • Canva and Google Slides add-ons.

Practical use cases

  • Voicing a training module synced to slides
  • producing an explainer video voiceover without a studio
  • replacing a poorly recorded voiceover using the voice changer
  • localising a presentation into several languages.

Who is it for?

  • L&D and corporate training teams, marketing and product teams making explainer videos, podcasters, small businesses.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium per-seat subscription with monthly voice-generation minutes

Plans described in the source

Free with roughly 10 minutes of voice generation and no downloads. Creator around $29/mo ($19 annually) with roughly 24 hours/year of generation, 1 seat. Growth around $99/mo ($66 annually) with roughly 96 hours/year and 3 seats. Business around $149/mo ($99 annually) with higher volume and 5 seats. Enterprise custom with unlimited generation, SSO and dedicated support. Murf API priced separately by characters.

Free plan

Yes - free tier with roughly 10 minutes of generation, but downloads are blocked.

Free trial

Free tier serves as the trial; paid trials occasionally offered.

Usage limits to consider

Metered by minutes/hours of generated voice per year rather than per month on some tiers. Free tier cannot download output. Seat counts are tier-limited. Voice changer minutes are separately capped.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The timeline editor synced to slides and video is the real differentiator - it is a production tool rather than a TTS endpoint
  • word-level pitch, pause and emphasis control gives directorial precision that most TTS tools lack
  • the voice changer is genuinely useful for salvaging bad recordings
  • substantially cheaper than ElevenLabs at business volumes.

Limitations to consider

  • Voice naturalness is clearly a step below ElevenLabs, particularly on emotional delivery
  • no voice cloning of arbitrary voices on standard tiers
  • Arabic voice quality and selection are limited
  • the annual-hours metering model is unusual and easy to misjudge
  • free tier cannot download, so real evaluation requires paying.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web (Murf Studio)
  • Chrome extension
  • Google Slides add-on
  • Canva app
  • API

Languages

  • 20+ languages including Arabic and French; 200+ voices

API access

Yes - Murf API with character-based pricing, separate from Studio plans

Integrations and exports

  • Google Slides, Canva, PowerPoint (import), Adobe Audition (export), Zapier, YouTube

Evaluation notes

Compare a 60-second Arabic sample against ElevenLabs before choosing - Murf's language quality is uneven outside English. The slide-sync workflow is what justifies it over a raw TTS API.
